The '''2009–10''' season of the '''[[Belgian Pro League]]''' (also known as ''Jupiler Pro League'' for sponsorship reasons) was the 107th season of top-tier football in [[Belgium]]. The season began on 31 July 2009 with the first matches of the regular season, and ended in May 2010 with the last matches of the playoff round. [[Standard Liège]] were the defending champions.

The competition underwent a significant overhaul for this season by reducing the number of teams and, for the first time in the history of the league, introducing a playoff system to determine the Belgian champions.

On April 18, 2010, [[R.S.C. Anderlecht|Anderlecht]] became champions as a result of a 1–2 victory in [[Bruges]] against one of their main rivals, [[Club Brugge K.V.|Club Brugge]].

==Changes from 2008–09==

===Structural changes===
The league size has been reduced from eighteen to sixteen teams. Further, the competition has been split into two stages, a conventional season and playoffs.

The participating clubs will first play a conventional [[Round-robin tournament|round-robin]] schedule for a total of 30 matches. After the conclusion of those matches, the team ranked 16th will be directly relegated to the [[Belgian Second Division]], while every other team will play in a playoff round according to its league table position.

The first six teams will play in the [[#Championship Playoff|Championship playoff]]. Points earned during the regular season are halved with an odd number of points being rounded up. The round will be played on a round-robin schedule. The winner of this round has won the Belgian championship and will participate in the [[2010–11 UEFA Champions League#Third qualifying round|third qualifying round]] of the 2010–11 UEFA Champions League. The runners-up will also play in the third qualifying round of the Champions League, while the third-placed team will enter the [[2010–11 UEFA Europa League#Third qualifying round|third qualifying round]] of the 2010–11 UEFA Europa League. Finally, the fourth-placed team will have to compete in a single match (called ''Testmatch'') against the winner of the Europa League playoff (see below) for one spot in the [[2010–11 UEFA Europa League#Second qualifying round|second qualifying round]] of the UEFA Europa League.

The teams finishing seventh through fourteenth will play in the [[#Europa League Playoff|Europa League playoff]] and start with zero points. The round will be played in two groups, with teams in positions 7, 9, 12 and 14 comprising Group A, and the remaining teams comprising Group B. Each group will be played on a round-robin schedule. The winners of these groups will then compete in a two-legged series to earn the right to play against the fourth-placed team of the Championship playoff for one spot in the second qualifying round of the UEFA Europa League.

The 15th-placed team will participate in the [[Belgian Second Division final rounds 2001–10#2010|Relegation playoff]], along with the teams ranked second through fifth in the [[2009–10 in Belgian football|Belgian Second Division]]. The winners of the playoff will earn a place in the [[2010–11 Belgian First Division]].

===Team changes===
* [[RAEC Mons (1910)|Mons]] and [[A.F.C. Tubize|Tubize]] were relegated.
* [[K. Sint-Truidense V.V.|Sint-Truiden]] was promoted.
* [[K.S.V. Roeselare|Roeselare]] beat [[F.C. Verbroedering Dender E.H.|Dender]], [[Lierse S.K. (1906)|Lierse]] and [[Royal Antwerp FC|Antwerp]] in the [[Belgian Second Division final round 2001-2010#2009|playoffs]] and was thus allowed to remain in the league. Dender was relegated while Lierse and Antwerp remained in the second division.

==Regular season==

===Financial troubles of Mouscron===
During the season, [[R.E. Mouscron|Mouscron]] got into financial trouble. This caused months of debate and several law procedures, with the fate of Mouscron changing from week to week. The board of Mouscron finally accepted the bankruptcy of Mouscron on 28 December 2009.<ref name=mouscronannulled/> At that point, the last two matches of Mouscron had already been forfeited as many players refused to play due to wages from November and December not being paid;<ref name=mouscron1>{{cite news |title=Mouscron players refuse to play |url=http://www.sporza.be/permalink/1.675647
|publisher=sporza.be |language=Dutch |date=2009-12-26}}</ref><ref name=mouscron2>
{{cite news |title=Mouscron forfeits game |url=http://sporza.be/cm/sporza/voetbal/Jupiler_Pro_League/091219_Moeskroen_forfait |publisher=sporza.be |language=Dutch |date=2009-12-19 |access-date=2009-12-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091222030502/http://sporza.be/cm/sporza/voetbal/Jupiler_Pro_League/091219_Moeskroen_forfait |archive-date=2009-12-22 |url-status=dead }}
</ref> three forfeits in a row would have also caused immediate elimination and relegation to the [[Belgian Third Division]].

As a result of the bankruptcy and relegation, Mouscron's record was expunged.<ref name=mouscronannulled/>

===Positions by round===
Note: The classification was made after the weekend (or midweek) of each matchday, so postponed matches were only processed at the time they were played to represent the ''real'' evolution in standings. The postponed matches are:
* Matchday 19: Mechelen vs. Germinal Beerschot of 18 December,<ref>
{{cite news |title=KV Mechelen-G.Beerschot postponed |url=http://sporza.be/cm/sporza/voetbal/Jupiler_Pro_League/091217_afgelastingen |publisher=sporza.be |language=Dutch |date=2009-12-17 |access-date=2009-12-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091219133835/http://www.sporza.be/cm/sporza/voetbal/Jupiler_Pro_League/091217_afgelastingen |archive-date=2009-12-19 |url-status=dead }}
</ref> Charleroi vs. Standard and Anderlecht vs. Club Brugge  of 20 December.<ref>{{cite news |title=Snow makes it impossible for football |url=http://sporza.be/cm/sporza/voetbal/Jupiler_Pro_League/091219_charleroi_standard_vooraf# |publisher=sporza.be |language=Dutch |date=2009-12-19 |access-date=2009-12-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091221180131/http://www.sporza.be/cm/sporza/voetbal/Jupiler_Pro_League/091219_charleroi_standard_vooraf |archive-date=2009-12-21 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The matches will be played in the beginning of February, between the 24th and 25th matchday.<ref>{{cite news |title=Anderlecht and Brugge meet on 3 February |url=http://www.sporza.be/permalink/1.675087
|publisher=sporza.be |language=Dutch |date=2009-12-24}}</ref>
* Matchday 22: Club Brugge vs. Westerlo of 16 January<ref name=ppd1601>{{cite news |title=Club Brugge - Westerlo cancelled |url=http://www.sporza.be/permalink/1.696016
|publisher=sporza.be |language=Dutch |date=2010-01-16}}</ref> which was played during the 24th matchday on 30 January.<ref name=ppdtomd24>{{cite news |title=Club Brugge - Westerlo postponed to 30 January |url=http://www.sporza.be/permalink/1.698095
|publisher=sporza.be |language=Dutch |date=2010-01-30}}</ref>
* Matchday 23: Cercle Brugge vs. Charleroi of 23 January (as a result of the first leg of the quarter final of the [[2009–10 Belgian Cup|Belgian Cup]] between Anderlecht and Cercle Brugge being played on this date<ref name=belgianfootballisafarce>{{cite news |title=Cup duel between Anderlecht and Cercle Brugge played over two legs after all |url=http://www.sporza.be/permalink/1.699899 |publisher=sporza.be |language=Dutch |date=2010-01-21}}</ref>). The new date for this match is 24 February, between matchdays 27 and 28.
* Matchday 24: Sint-Truiden vs. Westerlo of 30 January (as a result of the postponement of the match Club Brugge vs. Westerlo to this date) is postponed to 3 February,<ref name=ppdtomd24/> which is between matchdays 24 and 25. Because of snowfall, both Roeselare vs. Genk and Charleroi vs. Lokeren were postponed.<ref>{{cite news |title=Roeselare-Genk and Charleroi-Lokeren cancelled |url=http://www.sporza.be/permalink/1.706194 |publisher=sporza.be |language=Dutch |date=2010-01-30}}</ref> The match Charleroi vs. Lokeren was originally scheduled to be played on February 10 between matchdays 25 and 26, but was postponed again because of more snow <ref name=ppdagain>{{cite news |title=Postponed match Charleroi-Lokeren cancelled again |url=http://www.sporza.be/permalink/1.713825 |publisher=sporza.be |language=Dutch |date=2010-02-10}}</ref> and will now be played on March 10 between matchdays 28 and 29.<ref name=rescheduledmatches>{{cite news |title=Charleroi receives Anderlecht on March 6th |url=http://www.sporza.be/permalink/1.723268 |publisher=sporza.be |language=Dutch |date=2010-02-23}}</ref> Roeselare vs. Genk was rescheduled to 24 February, between matchdays 27 and 28.
* Matchday 26: Yet again snow caused several matches to be postponed, in this case Mechelen-Genk, Cercle Brugge-Lokeren, Charleroi-Anderlecht and Germinal Beerschot-Zulte-Waregem.<ref name=4matches>{{cite news |title=Winter weather messes up 26th matchday |url=http://www.sporza.be/permalink/1.715730 |publisher=sporza.be |language=Dutch |date=2010-02-13}}</ref> All matches were rescheduled to be played during the weekend of the 29th matchday, on March 6 and 7.<ref name=rescheduledmatches/>
* Matchday 29: Due to the rescheduling of several matches to the first weekend of March,<ref name=rescheduledmatches/> when this matchday was to be played, the whole matchday was postponed one week. With both [[R.S.C. Anderlecht|Anderlecht]] and [[Standard Liège]] still playing in the [[2009–10 UEFA Europa League|UEFA Europa League]] on Thursdays, all matches will be played on Sunday 14 March at 20:00.<ref name=europaleague>{{cite news |title=Play-offs 1 will start one week later on 27/03 |url=http://www.sporza.be/permalink/1.725788 |publisher=sporza.be |language=Dutch |date=2010-02-13}}</ref>
* Matchday 30: With matchday 29 moved to 14 March, matchday 30 was also rescheduled, to Sunday 21 March.<ref name=europaleague/>

On top of that, the results of [[R.E. Mouscron|Mouscron]] were annulled between matchdays 20 and 21, causing many shifts between those matchdays.<ref name=mouscronannulled/> Also, for the rest of the season, there will be no point at which all teams have played the same number of matches, until at the end.

==Championship playoff==
The points obtained during the regular season were halved (and rounded up) before the start of the playoff. Thus, Anderlecht started with 35 points, Club Brugge with 29, Gent with 25, Kortrijk 23 and both Sint-Truiden and Zulte-Waregem started with 21.

===Europa League playoff final===
The winners of both playoff groups will compete in a two-legged match. The winners on [[Aggregate score#Total points series (aggregate)|aggregate]] will compete in another match (called ''Testmatch'') against a team from the championship playoff (see below). If both teams are tied after two matches, the [[away goals rule]] will be applied. Should both teams still be tied afterwards, thirty minutes of [[extra time]] will be played and, if necessary, a [[Penalty shootout (association football)|penalty shootout]] will be conducted.

===Testmatches Europa League===
The fourth-placed team from the championship playoff and the winners of the Europa League playoff competed for one spot in the [[2010–11 UEFA Europa League#Third qualifying round|third qualifying round]] of the 2010–11 UEFA Europa League.

Note: The spot in the [[2010–11 UEFA Europa League#Third qualifying round|second qualifying round]] of the 2010–11 UEFA Europa League was taken by [[Cercle Brugge KSV|Cercle Brugge]], who was the runners-up of the [[2009–10 Belgian Cup]] to Champions League-qualified [[K.A.A. Gent|Gent]].
